title: Give the button three tiers
prompt:
The primitives are done, but `.nw-button` reaches straight for `--nw-blue-600`, so no theme can ever change it. Add the two missing tiers:

1. On `:root`, declare the semantic tokens `--nw-color-action-bg` and `--nw-color-action-text`, pointing at the right primitives.
2. On `.nw-button`, declare the component tokens `--nw-button-bg` and `--nw-button-text`, pointing at the semantic tokens, and use them for `background` and `color`.

The button must look exactly as it does now, and no `.nw-button` rule may mention a `--nw-blue-…` or `--nw-white` primitive.
hints: Semantic tokens look like `--nw-color-action-bg: var(--nw-blue-600);` inside `:root`.
Component tokens go inside the `.nw-button { … }` rule, not on `:root`, so they resolve on each button.
Then change `background: var(--nw-blue-600)` to `background: var(--nw-button-bg)`, and the same for `color`.
explanation: The button now resolves `--nw-button-bg` → `--nw-color-action-bg` → `--nw-blue-600`. Because the component tokens are declared on `.nw-button`, each button looks up the semantic token from its own ancestors, so setting `--nw-color-action-bg` on `.promo` re-colors only the promo button. Had you declared `--nw-button-bg` on `:root`, the value would be computed once at the root and the promo override would do nothing.

checks.still-blue: The button still renders blue with white text
checks.follows-semantic: Overriding `--nw-color-action-bg` on `.promo` re-colors only the promo button
checks.no-primitives: No `.nw-button` rule references a primitive token
